questions.question: How is student safety best maintained on a school bus?

options.text: Keep students on the bus.
Let some students get off while others stay on.
Let all students get off the bus.
Create panic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest when they stay on the bus and remain under control.

questions.question: What happens if you exit the vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
That exercise is reset.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
One point is subtracted from your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting the vehicle, you must face the vehicle and use three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly results in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: What does the overhead inside rearview mirror do?

options.text: It lets the driver see inside the bus.
It lets the driver see outside the bus.
It monitors traffic.
It opens and closes the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the driver see inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror helps the driver watch what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: When should outside mirrors on a school bus be adjusted?

options.text: Before the trip starts.
During the trip.
After students get on the bus.
After the trip ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip starts.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving. Proper mirror adjustment is critical for the safety of students and other drivers.

questions.question: What should a student do if they drop something near a stopped bus?

options.text: Quickly pick up the item.
Leave the item behind.
Ask the driver to pick it up.
Have another student pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could disappear from the driver's view. Instead, students should move away from the bus's danger zones, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: What should a student do if they drop something while walking toward the bus?

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.
Leave the item and walk away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could disappear from the driver's view. Instead, students should move away from the bus's danger zones, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: What should a driver check before leaving a bus stop?

options.text: No students are running to catch the bus.
Students have placed backpacks in the aisle.
Students have opened the emergency vent.
Students are facing the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: No students are running to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Before pulling away from a bus stop, make sure no students are running to catch the bus.

questions.question: What is true about loading and unloading a school bus?

options.text: It can be dangerous for passengers.
It does not need supervision.
It should be done while refueling.
The driver can talk to other drivers during this time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding on the bus. Drivers must follow safety procedures and supervise these activities carefully.

questions.question: What is true about pull-ups during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Points are subtracted for each pull-up.
A driver can do three pull-ups per maneuver without penalty.
A pull-up earns points only if the driver exits before pulling up.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: The first pull-up has no penalty. However, doing too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must fit completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a backing maneuver you will do on the basic control skills test?

options.text: Straight line backing
Offset back/right
Offset back/left
Blind offset

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind offset
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, you should check that:

options.text: The lift is loosely attached.
The lift is not leaking.
The lift is fully extended.
The lift is the proper color.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection test, check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and latched securely.

questions.question: ABS helps you to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Stay in control on slippery roads.
Drive longer distances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in control on slippery roads.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces. You should drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings:

options.text: Have control devices.
Do not have control devices.
Should be avoided.
Usually have a flagger directing traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. It is your responsibility as a driver to decide when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: When stopped at a railroad crossing while driving a school bus, you should:

options.text: Assume you will hear an approaching train.
Only rely on signals to tell you if a train is coming.
Open the door and listen for a train.
Move forward immediately after a train passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the door and listen for a train.
questions.explanation: When stopped at a railroad crossing in a school bus, do not rely only on signals. Tell all passengers to be quiet, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. Before crossing, check for trains coming from both directions.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must show each of the following, except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge works.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating range, if equipped.
That the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works correctly. The gauge should show normal oil pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If equipped, the oil temperature gauge should gradually rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: When inspecting engine belts during the vehicle inspection test:

options.text: Each belt should have up to three inches of play.
You do not need to identify the water pump belt.
You should remove the air compressor belt.
You must identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Each belt should have up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them and make sure they are working, not damaged or leaking, and mounted securely.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: Backing a school bus is:

options.text: Strongly encouraged.
Strongly discouraged.
Only done in the morning.
Only done with students guiding you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged. Only back up if there is no other way to move the vehicle.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before making a turn, you should:

options.text: Skid to a stop.
Stop past the stop line for a better view.
Let your vehicle roll.
Keep the front wheels straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight ahead and do not let your vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can still see its rear tires.
